societies.name: Riverworld — The common grail provision system
societies.society: Resurrected humans with keyed access to regular technological rations

scope.continuity: Farmer’s original published book-series shared grail mechanism
scope.period: Established riverbank settlements while the regular grail system operates
scope.population: Living resurrected human inhabitants with active personal grails
exclusions: Every local kingdom as identically free or secure
Television or game adaptations without separate verification

societies.description:
Riverworld’s residents receive keyed grails that supply food, drink, cloth and discretionary goods when connected to regularly powered grailstones. Subsistence production is therefore technologically supplied rather than bought through necessary agricultural labor. Access begins widely distributed, but it is not secure in every community: grails can be lost, and captors can force owners to surrender their contents. Guarantees are moderately favorable for the common mechanism, with a broad interval reflecting those real failures.

Individual keys give residents access without giving them control over the sustaining infrastructure. Its creators and administrators belong to the Ethical project, whose biological alien and human-derived participants prevent a simple machine-sovereignty inference. Control remains unresolved, and the guaranteed-provider classification is provisional. Resurrection does not make dead stored personas active leisure residents. Inhabited communities still build, govern, travel, create and care for one another, while enslaved residents may perform additional coerced labor. Daily rations and an adult-looking resurrected population do not provide an all-person nonworking percentage.

guarantees.basis: Personal grails actually provide recurring food/drink/cloth without wage purchases, but loss and grail slavery undermine effective security.

control.basis: Keys confer access rather than infrastructure ownership; Ethical creator/administrator origins are mixed biological alien and human-derived, not simply an autonomous AI provider.

nonworking.basis: Building, governance, care and coerced labor continue; only active living resurrected humans are counted, and no participation census is available.

exclusions: Regular lockstep-cycle communities already retained as lockstep-individual-robot-economy

societies.description:
Earth’s recognized Million inherit a permanently awake estate society whose robots supply their ordinary needs. The publisher and author establish the closed population boundary and hereditary privilege; the named review supplies the actual robot provisioning. Guarantees are favorably estimated inside the recognized estate population, with broad uncertainty about legal security and individual dependence. Unauthorized additional people are hunted rather than included. Sleeping visitors do not enlarge the active leisure denominator.

This differs from the retained regular Lockstep communities: its institutional unit is an enforced permanent caste controlling Earth’s estates, rather than ordinary cycle participants accumulating robot output and income during hibernation. Productive authority is spread among human estate families while concentrated through inherited property and population policing. The control estimate is consequently mixed, with shared-proprietor and elite interpretations both visible. Care, policing, education and estate management remain useful work. Robot servants and a privileged way of life do not establish that every recognized resident ceases all useful activity; nonworking remains unresolved.

control.basis: Multiple human estate families own the productive setting, but hereditary concentration and population enforcement qualify distributed control.

review_notes: Third expansion tranche was saved before analysis. Eight ordered dispositions add two provisional records; ambiguous leads are skipped after bounded references.
Riverworld’s grail access is real but can be captured or lost; the shared mechanism is counted once and local oppression is not erased.
